q: Which correctly matches a compound made from Calvin cycle products with its extra requirement and its use?
options: Cellulose – needs phosphate from the soil – used as the main energy store
Starch – needs nitrogen absorbed from the soil – used to build plant cell walls
Amino acids – need nitrogen (and sulfur for some) – used to make proteins
Sucrose – needs magnesium – used as a structural protein in membranes
explanation: Starch (storage) and cellulose (cell walls) are glucose polymers made from TP and need no minerals; sucrose is the soluble transport sugar in phloem. Amino acids are built from carbon skeletons derived from Calvin cycle (and respiratory) intermediates plus ammonium from nitrate; cysteine and methionine also need sulfur. Phospholipids and nucleic acids need phosphate; chlorophyll needs magnesium.
